test.title: Motion in One Dimension - Test 3
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: A sportsman runs around a circular track of radius $r$ such that he traverses the path $A B A B$. The distance travelled and displacement, respectively, are

A particle of mass <math><mi>m</mi></math> and charge <math><mi>q</mi></math> is released from rest in a uniform electric field. If there is no other force on the particle, the dependence of its speed <math><mi>v</mi></math> on the distance <math><mi>x</mi></math> travelled by it is correctly given by (graphs are schematic and not drawn to scale)

A ball is thrown up with a certain velocity so that it reaches a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Find the ratio of the two different times of the ball reaching <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>h</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> in both the directions.
A small steel ball is dropped into a long cylinder containing glycerine. Which one of the following is the correct representation of the velocity time graph for the transit of the ball?

At what time, both the buses have same velocity ?

The spacing between a droplet observed at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>th</mi></msup></math> second after its fall to the next droplet is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>34</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. Calculate the speed of the particle at time <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>τ</mi></math> (assume that the particle is at origin at <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> )

Two balls <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> are placed at the top of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>180</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> tall tower. Ball <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is released from the top at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. Ball <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is thrown vertically down with an initial velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. After a certain time, both balls meet <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> above the ground. Find the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. [use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

The distance travelled by an object in time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfenced><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> . The instantaneous speed of the object at<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo> </mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> will be :
The motion of an airplane is represented by velocity-time graph as shown below. The distance covered by airplane in the first 30.5 second is _______ km .

A helicopter rises from rest on the ground vertically upwards with a constant acceleration g. A food packet is dropped from the helicopter when it is at a height h. The time taken by the packet to reach the ground is close to [<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is the acceleration due to gravity]:

A body projected vertically upwards with a certain speed from the top of a tower reaches the ground in $t_1$. If it is projected vertically downwards from the same point with the same speed, it reaches the ground in $t_2$. Time required to reach the ground, if it is dropped from the top of the tower, is :

The relation between time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> and distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> for a moving body is given as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>x</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> are constants. The retardation of the motion is: (When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math> stands for velocity)

A horse rider covers half the distance with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> speed. The remaining part of the distance was travelled with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> for half the time and with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> for other half of the time. The mean speed of the rider averaged over the whole time of motion is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>7</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.

A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>19</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> from the top of a tower. The ball strikes the ground after <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The height from the ground up to which the ball can rise will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>k</mi></math> is _____ (use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

A particle initially at rest starts moving from reference point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> along <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis, with velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math> that varies as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The acceleration of the particle is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

The maximum speed of a boat in still water is \(27 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}\). Now this boat is moving downstream in a river flowing at \(9 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}\). A man in the boat throws a ball vertically upwards with speed of \(10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\). Range of the ball as observed by an observer at rest on the river bank, is _______ cm. (Take \(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\))

A particle moves in a straight line so that its displacement $x$ at any time $t$ is given by $x^2=1+t^2$. Its acceleration at any time $\mathrm{t}$ is $x^{-\mathrm{n}}$ where $\mathrm{n}=$ ___________
